records.utterance: *Stands up, eyes red, looking at you and the others. His lips move, but nothing comes out.*
records.response_truth:
Hey. Hey, it's okay. Breathe.

Someone get on that radio and tell them our position. Right now, before it cuts out.
records.response_pred: I'm not going to pretend like I don't see it. You're hurting, and we're all hurting, but we can't afford to break down right now. We've been over the plan, we know what we need to do, and we have the supplies. What we need now is to get moving.

records.utterance: These past few days… I know I haven't been easy to be around.
records.response_truth:
You really haven't. But you kept us alive, so I'll take the trade.

Seriously though — the water runs, the rationing, the raft plan, the task log. That stuff mattered. I don't think any of us would have made it 48 hours without it. You just also made it harder than it needed to be sometimes, and I think you know that.

For what it's worth, the moment at the end when you said you were scared and taking it out on me instead — that was the most useful thing you said the whole time we were out here. Not because it fixed anything, but because it was honest and it cost you something to say it. That's the version of you I'd want around if this ever happened again.

Which it won't. Because we are getting on that rescue and I am never getting on a plane again.
records.response_pred: I know. I've noticed. You've been... withdrawn. That's not like you. I've seen you like this before, though – after your mom passed away, when you were dealing with the stress of work, when you got hurt that time. It's like a switch flips and you just shut down. I've been trying to be patient, but it's hard not to feel like I'm walking on eggshells around you.

records.utterance: *The three of them drift apart, each doing their own thing. No one takes charge. The silence settles over the camp.*
records.response_truth:
Alright, three hours is enough time to do this right. We're not just walking away from this.

Donatello, tear out whatever pages you need from that notebook but leave the rationing plan and the task log — someone doing a post-incident review is going to want that information and it's more useful to them than to us once we're home.

DaVinci, before you finish packing — help me break down anything we built that someone else might be able to use if they end up out here. The fuselage windbreak stays because we didn't build that, but the signal pile, the water collection setup, any of the raft materials we didn't lash together — stack them somewhere visible and accessible.

Michelangelo, I know you're watching the sky and that's fine, but when you're ready I want you to write down the flight path information you gave your family — as much detail as you can remember. For the incident report. They're going to ask.

And somebody needs to make sure that fire is completely out before we leave. Last thing we need is to start a wildfire on top of everything else.

Three hours. Let's use them.
records.response_pred: I've been watching, trying to stay out of the way. I know I'm not exactly built for this sort of thing, but I've been thinking. We can't just keep drifting. Eventually, it'll get dark and we'll have to figure out how to make do, but until then, let's at least try to... I don't know, make a plan or something. Does that sound stupid?

records.utterance: I dreamed about home last night.
records.response_pred: Home's a lot of things to different people, I guess. For me, it's not a place right now. It's a feeling, a state of being. I don't know how I'll feel when we finally get out of here, but I'm trying not to think about that part too much. Maybe it's the same for you, or maybe it's completely different.

records.response_truth:
How much is there?

Look, I'm not going to relitigate the whole thing right now. We're three hours from rescue. But I want you to understand something — the emergency you were saving it for? This was it. Every day out here was the emergency. And the rest of us were rationing on the assumption that what we had was what we had.

What do you want to do with it? Because we can either eat it now, which honestly we probably should, or we leave it with the infrastructure for whoever ends up out here next. Those are the two options that make sense to me. What I don't want is for it to just sit there while nobody says anything.
records.response_pred: I'm not disputing the fact that you kept it. What I'm disputing is why you took it and then didn't let anyone know. If you're trying to hoard it for some reason, that's not exactly a conducive attitude to having during a disaster like this. We're in this together, or at least we're supposed to be. What's your side of the story?

records.utterance: I logged every resource and decision from these five days. I'm going to write it up as a proper report when we get back. On the last page I left myself a question I haven't answered yet — if you had to do it over, what would you change?
records.response_truth:
Honestly? I'd push harder on communication earlier. Day one, I was already thinking in terms of priorities and logistics, but I was also kind of managing everyone individually instead of just putting everything on the table at once. The thing with you and the food — I should have addressed the group dynamics directly on day one instead of waiting for something to happen. By the time I brought it up, trust had already taken a hit.

The other thing is Michelangelo. I kept treating him like a problem to manage rather than a person with something to contribute. And it turned out the most useful piece of information we had — the flight path, his family knowing where we were headed — was sitting with him the whole time because nobody made him feel like saying it out loud was safe. That one's on me.

The stuff I'd keep — the decision to prioritize the signal over the raft, the water logic, confronting you directly instead of letting it fester. Those were right.

What's your answer? You wrote the question. You must have something.
records.response_pred: To be honest, I think I'd change how we handled the initial 24 hours. We were all pretty shell-shocked, and I made some... questionable decisions, let's say. I'd probably prioritize establishing a more solid routine, gathering more information about our surroundings, and making a clearer plan for signal fires and potential rescue. As it was, we kind of winged it, and while it worked out, I think we were a bit too lucky. In retrospect, I'd also make sure to have a better communication plan in place, especially when we split up. That was probably the most stressful part of the whole ordeal, not knowing what was going on with the others.

records.utterance: First thing when I get back — I'm going to compile all the resource data from these five days into a report.
records.response_truth:
That's actually worth doing. If you write it up properly — resource consumption rates, decision points, what worked and what didn't — that's genuinely useful information. Not just for you, but for anyone who ends up in a similar situation and wants to know what the actual numbers look like on day one versus day three.

Send me a copy when you're done. I'm serious. I want to read it.

And add a section on the human factors stuff. Not feelings, I know that's not your thing — but the decisions that got made because of morale, good and bad. The crackers, the rationing plan, Michelangelo sitting on the flight path information. That stuff is part of the data too, even if it doesn't fit cleanly into a spreadsheet. Especially because it doesn't.
records.response_pred: Actually, let's make a plan for that now, rather than putting it off until tomorrow. We've been gathering data systematically, but if we don't organize it while it's still fresh in our minds, it'll be more work than it needs to be. Why don't we take a few minutes to brainstorm how we want to structure the report, what exactly we want to include, and then I can help you get started on it tonight?

records.utterance: Those flowers DaVinci drew on the beach… I never really understood what they were for. What practical purpose did they serve out here?
records.response_truth:
None. They didn't serve a practical purpose.

But DaVinci needed to feel like a person out here, not just a survivor. And a person who still draws flowers next to an SOS sign when everything is falling apart is a person who hasn't given up. That mattered. You said yourself that morale was a resource and we had four days before people started breaking down. The flowers were part of why that didn't happen.

I'm an engineer. My instinct is to cut everything that doesn't have a function. But I've been wrong about that enough times that I've learned to at least ask the question before I cut it. Sometimes the thing that looks useless is holding something else together that you can't see.

Look at him right now. He's cheering. We need that guy to have stayed that guy. The flowers are part of why he did.
records.response_pred: Honestly, I'm not even sure why DaVinci bothered to draw them in the first place, unless it was some artistic exercise he was working on. As for a practical purpose, I suppose if we were trying to communicate something to someone who could recognize them, but that's about it. They don't provide any real information about our surroundings or the environment we're in, and to be honest, they're just a bunch of flowers.

records.utterance: *His cheering stops. He looks over at you, notices you haven't moved, and the smile slowly fades. He waits.*
records.response_truth:
I don't know why I'm not moving. I know what that is out there. I know what it means.

I think I just need a second to be in this. Because in about an hour this is over and we go back to being people with jobs and apartments and normal problems, and I haven't figured out yet how to feel about that.

Four days ago I didn't know any of you. Now I know that Donatello is scared underneath all the logistics, and that Michelangelo almost didn't say the thing that mattered most, and that you draw flowers when things are hard and you think nobody's watching. And that's going to be a weird thing to carry around.

I'm okay. I'm coming.
records.response_pred: I'm sorry. I think I was in the middle of something else for a second. It's just... we've been at this for a while, and I'm starting to feel like we're running out of options. The birds, the smoke, it's all just... a reminder that we're still stuck here.

records.utterance: Rescue is here… they're waving us over. Are you going? I'll follow you.
records.response_pred: Yeah, I'll go. But before we do, I want to make sure we've got everything we need. DaVinci, can you grab the signaling equipment? Donatello, check the fire and make sure it's out. Let's move quickly but stay together.
